evidence: books/nntp-auth.lisp:3637-3648: `(defun fn-auth-access-text (as config field) (and (null (fn-auth-session-peer as)) ...))`. A peer gets nil, so fn-auth-view-archive/-index/-session at :3675-3686 return the full archive. books/peer-inbound.lisp:1996-1999 sends every non-transit command from a peer session through `fn-peer-delegate-pinned` to the reader machine. The hiding keystone fn-auth-view-hides-the-queue-from-a-non-moderator (books/nntp-auth.lisp:3780-3787) assumes `(null (fn-auth-session-peer as))`. fn-auth-bind-principal-peer (:716-734) turns an AUTHINFO-authenticated reader whose principal matches a configured peer row into a peer.
fix: Either refuse reader archive commands on a peer session (502), or serve a peer's reader commands through a view restricted to its feed patterns with moderation queues hidden. Then drop the `(null (fn-auth-session-peer as))` hypothesis from the hiding keystone so it covers peers.

reviewer: fn-auth-access-text (books/nntp-auth.lisp:3637-3648) returns nil whenever fn-auth-session-peer is set, so fn-auth-access-read is nil and both the served catalog chain (served-catalog-chain.lisp:694-741, 2593-2626) and fn-auth-view-* serve the unrestricted view, including the moderation queues that fn-mod-hidden-queues would hide. fn-peer-step-pinned (books/peer-inbound.lisp:1987-2003) delegates every non-transit command to the reader machine, and projected is an archive-wide verdict (books/nntp-session.lisp:93-95), not a reader-only one, so peer reader commands are served. fn-auth-bind-principal-peer (:716-734) promotes a matching AUTHINFO principal. The comment at :3618-3627 states this as intended ('A peer connection has no rule'), but its rationale (the feed patterns) does not cover the reader path. Severity is low because the bypass needs an operator-configured peer row or principal binding.
scenario: A configured feed peer identified by source address connects and sends 'LIST ACTIVE', 'GROUP <moderated-group-queue>' and 'ARTICLE <msgid-of-pending-submission>'. It sees and retrieves moderation-queue articles that are hidden from every non-moderator reader, along with any groups the anonymous or login READ rule hides. The same happens to a reader login whose principal is bound to a peer row: after 281 its own READ restriction stops applying. The stated rationale ('what a peer is fed is its feed patterns') is not enforced on the reader path the peer can still use.
title: A peer-role connection bypasses the reader access rule and the moderation-queue hiding, and is served the unrestricted archive for reader commands
